scholarships.title: Mauritius-Africa Scholarship Scheme (MASS)
scholarships.official_source: Ministry of Tertiary Education, Science and Research, Republic of Mauritius

existing.description: The Mauritius-Africa Scholarship Scheme is the Government of Mauritius scholarship for African students, run by the Ministry of Tertiary Education, Science and Research and open to resident citizens of African Union member states and African Commonwealth countries. The 2026 edition funds Diploma, Bachelor's, MPhil and PhD study at public higher education institutions in Mauritius, paying tuition and course-related costs up to a published cap, a monthly living allowance of MUR 16,500 and a return airfare, while requiring awardees to have already secured or applied for a place at a listed Mauritian public institution. Applications are routed through a nominating agency in the applicant's own country, so the Ministry does not accept direct applications.
eligibility: Be a resident citizen of an African Union member state or an African Commonwealth country
For undergraduate programmes, be above 18 and not yet 26 on 1 January of the intake year
For MPhil, MPhil/PhD and PhD programmes, not yet 40 on 1 January of the intake year
Have already applied for a full-time on-campus Diploma, Degree, MPhil or PhD programme at a listed public higher education institution in Mauritius for the intake year
Hold a qualifying examination result with an overall average of about 60% or 12/20, or the A-level equivalent, or an equivalent qualification
Provide TOEFL 550 (paper), 213 (computer) or 79 (internet), or IELTS 5.5, where the language of instruction in the qualifying examination was not English
Not already hold an undergraduate degree when applying for an undergraduate programme
Not be a self-financing African student already studying in Mauritius applying for the same programme level
existing.eligibility_summary: Resident citizens of African Union member states or African Commonwealth countries aged between 18 and 26 for undergraduate programmes or under 40 for MPhil and PhD programmes by 1 January of the intake year, with a qualifying secondary or undergraduate result of about 60% or 12/20 or the equivalent, and holding or applying for a place at a listed Mauritian public higher education institution.
benefits: Annual payment of fees and study-related costs up to MUR 100,000 for beneficiaries from SADC countries and MUR 160,000 for beneficiaries from non-SADC countries
Monthly living allowance of MUR 16,500 credited monthly against evidence of attendance from the institution
Return airfare from the country of origin to Mauritius and back after successful completion of the scholarship period
Student visa and provisional entry permit arranged by the host institution
Refunded university application fee for successful applicants
coverage: Tuition fees and course-related costs up to a published annual cap
Return airfare by the most economical route to and from Mauritius
Student visa processing through the host institution and the Passport and Immigration Office
requirements: Submit the application through the nominating agency in your own country; applications not processed through a nominating agency are not considered
Obtain either a conditional offer from your chosen Mauritian public institution or proof of having paid its application fee
Produce original educational certificates in Mauritius within two weeks of arrival
Undergo a medical check-up in a Mauritian public hospital within one month of arrival
Not interrupt studies to take up employment, which terminates the award and requires refund of the whole amount paid
Inform the institution and the Ministry at least two weeks before any travel out of Mauritius
Ensure the host institution submits quarterly attendance and progress reports to support continued disbursement
documents: Certified copy of the biodata page of the passport
Conditional offer letter from a public higher education institution in Mauritius, or its application fee receipt
Medical certificate completed and stamped by a registered medical practitioner
existing.english_requirement: Where the language of instruction in the qualifying examination was not English, a valid TOEFL result of 550 paper-based, 213 computer-based or 79 internet-based, or IELTS 5.5, or another acceptable proof of English proficiency is required, and a virtual verbal interaction may be requested before the award
application_method: Apply to a listed Mauritian public higher education institution in parallel, through its own admission window
Complete the Mauritius-Africa Scholarship Application Form
Submit the form with all checklist documents to the nominating agency in your country of origin by that agency's deadline
The nominating agency endorses and transmits the application to the Ministry
After award, the host institution applies for the student visa and provisional entry permit
On arrival, produce original certificates, undergo the medical check-up and open a Mauritian bank account for the allowance
existing.selection_notes: Selection is on merit, after all attached conditions are satisfied and the host institution confirms a seat has been offered. Applications without endorsement from a nominating agency, or from the Ministry of Education where no agency exists, are not considered. Candidates not informed of selection within six months of the application deadline should consider themselves not selected, and the Ministry does not respond to individual queries. The final and binding decision on award rests with the Ministry of Tertiary Education, Science and Research, and the Government reserves the right to offer no scholarship at all following a call.
existing.best_fit: African Union and African Commonwealth nationals aged 18 to 26 (or under 40 for postgraduate study) who hold or have applied for a place at a Mauritian public institution and can obtain endorsement from their country's nominating agency.
existing.notes: Tuition and course-related costs are capped at MUR 100,000 per year for SADC beneficiaries and MUR 160,000 per year for non-SADC beneficiaries, on the rate basis published in the 2026 guidelines. Awardees must supplement the monthly allowance to cover living costs, must bear the cost of books and of examination re-sits or repeats, and are expected to arrive with funds for their one-way air ticket and at least USD 1,000 for the first three months.
existing.duration: Diploma up to three years, Bachelor's up to four years, MPhil up to two years plus six months for thesis defence, MPhil/PhD up to three years plus six months for the transfer report plus one year plus six months for the thesis defence, PhD up to three years plus six months
existing.application_period: Annual edition published by the Ministry, with applications made through the nominating agency in the applicant's country and in parallel with the chosen Mauritian public university's admission window
existing.deadline_display: No central date is published: each nominating agency sets its own deadline and communicates it to prospective applicants. For the 2026 edition the Mauritian public universities opened their own application windows from October 2025 and closed them between February and March 2026, so the next edition is expected to follow the same annual cycle.
